meta.what: B1: 90% bands for the cumulative 2022-2026 error of the no-war counterfactual, measured directly from the back-tests, per flow and size class, for 1-5 years ahead. B2: country-specific bands for Russia's neighbours tested on their own history. B3: Moldova's imports from Russia split into non-gas goods and right-bank Gazprom gas.
meta.units: Multipliers, real terms. cumulative_bands: multiplier on the SUM over the horizon of the expected (central) level: the no-war cumulative level lies in [low, high] x sum of central expected levels with ~90% probability. multiplier_vs_2021 per year as in counterfactual.json (2026 as an annual rate). EUR bn nominal where stated; USD converted at the yearly ECB average rates in the counterfactual inputs (2021 1.183).
meta.method: For each back-test (origins 2007, 2012, 2016) and country-flow, the cumulative ratio sum(w_h x actual_h) / sum(w_h x predicted_h) over h = 1..H, in real levels, for the chosen model (rw for to_rus and services, lin for from_rus and buy_ukr, rf for sell_ukr) and for rw (used for hubs, Belarus and non-reporters). Missing target years (2014-2015 in the 2013 test, 2020 in the 2016 test) are filled by interpolating that case's log error. 5th/50th/95th percentiles per flow x size class (thin-cell rule as in counterfactual.json), then multiplied in logs by K = 1.2, the factor at which quantiles from two tests cover 90% of the third (2008 and 2016 tests) for the 5-year sum.
meta.how_to_apply: In site/index.html spread(): replace ql/qh, now sums of yearly (e - ex(q_lo)), by ql = (1 - band.low) x SUM_i e_i and qh = (band.high - 1) x SUM_i e_i, where e_i = base x FRAC_i x bmul_i (central) and band = cumulative_bands[model][flow/size][H] with H = number of years summed (H5_2026_8of12 when 2026 enters at 8/12). The per-year bands stay for the yearly view (spreadYear/above3). Per-country entries in countries{} replace the generic per-year multipliers and cumulative bands for that flow (same structure as counterfactual.json plus cumulative_band).

from_rus.method: 2021 level held (random walk), country-specific interval: 5th-95th percentile of the country's own random-walk errors 1-5 years ahead (rolling origins 2005-2020, all years kept; the counterfactual's series and Russia's mirror report pooled), scaled by sqrt(h/3) and widened halfway to the block-bootstrap bounds, as belarus.json; used because its 2022-2026 cumulative band is at least 10% narrower than the generic one and its own held-out coverage holds

gas_right_bank.note: educated guess for the range (right-bank consumption 1.0-1.2 bcm a year before the war; weather and efficiency); same draw in every year

to_rus.method: 2021 level held (random walk) for non-gas goods with a Moldova-specific interval from its own 2002-2021 non-gas history (rolling origins, sqrt(h/3), widened halfway to block-bootstrap bounds); right-bank Gazprom gas at its 2019-2021 average volume (0.92 x 2021) and pre-war price; Transnistria's unpaid gas excluded from base and actuals alike; composite by Monte Carlo (non-gas errors correlated 0.7 between years, gas volume error persistent)

overlaps: No money amounts: this file only changes uncertainty bands (and Moldova's to_rus expected central from 1.00 to 0.973 x 2021). countries{} entries replace counterfactual.json per-country multipliers for those flows; they do not add to anything. Belarus keeps belarus.json. Moldova's to_rus actuals stay narrow.json's right-bank customs series; the Transnistria gas in energy2.json transit_gas high case must not be swapped back in (see notes).
notes: B1 finding: once calibrated to hold coverage out of sample, the directly measured cumulative band is about as wide as the current sum of yearly bands (width ratio 0.8-1.2; to_rus 0.98-1.14). Yearly errors of one country-flow are strongly correlated (mean 0.6-0.7 between years for goods), so adding yearly bands was close to right. The direct band is still the better rule, but it does not narrow the map materially.
Uncalibrated in-sample cumulative quantiles look 10-35% narrower, but cover only 84%/63%/85% of the held-out test; they should not be used.
The 2013 test (Russia-side shock 2014-2016) is covered at only 66% for 5-year sums even after calibration; services there at 34-44%, because only the 2008 test trains services for a 5-year sum.

MDA to_rus: base_range high (1.41) and years_hi 2022-2026 (2.95, 3.13, 1.36, 0.92, 0.76) in site/data.json come back from the energy2 transit_gas swap, which re-adds Transnistria gas in the high case after narrow.json removed it.
For rw flows the back-test errors already contain the risk that 2021 was an unusual year; the 2019-2021 alternative in base_range then counts that risk a second time.
